items.stem: You need the regional average sales to appear on every row regardless of the view's level of detail. Which Tableau feature is designed for this?

options.rationale: A basic aggregate follows the view's level of detail and cannot fix the granularity.
Correct: a FIXED LOD expression computes a value at a specified granularity independent of the view.
A filter limits data shown, it does not compute a fixed-level value.
A tooltip displays values; it does not compute them at a fixed level.

items.stem: What is the key difference between a join and a data blend in Tableau?

options.text: A join combines tables at the row level from (usually) the same source; a blend combines aggregated data from separate sources
options.rationale: Correct: joins merge rows typically within one connection, while blends combine aggregated results across different data sources on a linking field.
They behave differently at the row vs aggregate level.

options.text: A blend always runs faster than a join
options.rationale: Performance depends on the data, not a fixed rule.

options.text: A join can only use one field ever
options.rationale: Joins can use multiple key fields.

items.explanation: Correct: joins merge rows typically within one connection, while blends combine aggregated results across different data sources on a linking field.

items.stem: Which TWO are good practices when publishing a workbook to Tableau Cloud? (Select TWO)

options.text: Set permissions so only intended audiences can view the data
Configure an appropriate extract refresh schedule
options.rationale: Correct: scheduling refresh keeps published data current.

options.text: Publish with full access to all users by default
options.rationale: Default-open access can expose sensitive data.

options.text: Embed your personal password in the workbook
Delete the underlying data source after publishing
options.rationale: Removing the source breaks refresh and the workbook.

items.explanation: Both keyed options are correct; all-or-nothing scoring requires exactly the keyed set.
